messages:
Anna: quick note, saw a p99 jump for text-gen in eu-west this morning up to ~2.1s; queue grew but autoscaler didn't add pods fast enough. Heatmap shows empty spans in the 0.9s-1.4s buckets, looks like bucket sparsity

Kevin: can you paste the PromQL you used for the histogram? want to replicate in a debug panel

Anna: sure. i'm querying the runtime histogram like this:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool, region))
```

Anna: and queue by pool: 

```
sum(redwood_queue_depth{region=~"eu-west"}) by (pool)
```

Jules: empty buckets usually mean exporter bucket boundaries don't match request sizes OR we have an intermittent fast-path (local cache hits or compiled kernels) that skews the distribution. Any config change rolled overnight?

Anna: we rolled a light KV routing change to canaries at ~03:00Z, but this is on stable pools too. exporter buckets also show a gap — i'll attach the bucket list after lunch.

infra-alert-bot: Alert fired (eu-west): queue_surge for pool=gpu-xlarge at 2026-03-17T07:04:12Z :warning:

Kevin: autoscaler currently looks at 2m average queue depth. short tail bursts (20-90s) won't trip it. we should add a tail-aware trigger that looks at both a high quantile and a short-term max queue.

Jules: proposal: new autoscale condition = p95(latency) > 0.9s AND max_over_time(queue_depth[90s]) > 50 for 2m. prevents noise but captures tail-driven backpressure.

Suggested PromQL (draft):

```
(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool, region)) > 0.9)
and
(max_over_time(sum(redwood_queue_depth{region="eu-west"}) by (pool)[90s]) > 50)
```

Kevin: minor refinement: compute a short smoothing window for quantile to avoid scaling on a single scrape spike:

```
avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool, region))[1m:]) > 0.9
```

Anna: also asking for a "tail-gap" Grafana panel: p95 - p50 per pool over time. if that delta widens it's likely batching or cache miss pressure instead of steady load. panel query:

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool, region))
-
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool, region))
```

Jules: add a bucket-sparsity heatmap too: render buckets with counts per-le and highlight any empty buckets > 1m. that'll quickly point to exporter mismatch.

Kevin: ops constraints: when we roll the autoscale rule, limit scale-up to +30% replicas per 5m and add a cooldown of 3m after each scale event to avoid oscillation. also add a safety fallback: if p99 > 3s for >5m, force emergency scale +50%.

Anna: for reproducing, i'll run a short synthetic workload against eu-west canary. use this command in job-runner:

```
./tools/stress_client --model=text-gen --qps=45 --duration=600 --region=eu-west --seq-len=64,256 --randomize
```

Kevin: ping me before you start, i'll tail kube events, autoscaler logs and the node metrics.

Jules: i'll draft the infra PR with: new recording rules for p95/p50 per pool, the updated alert expression, grafana panels (tail-gap + bucket-sparsity), and autoscaler rate limits. will include a canary rollout plan and test harness instructions.

Anna: i'll also add an overlay panel in Grafana that shows last KV routing rollout timestamp (to correlate config flips). i'll export the histogram bucket boundaries into the panel so we can visually inspect gaps.

infra-alert-bot: autoscaler snapshot: pool=gpu-xlarge current=10 desired=10 last_scale=2026-03-17T06:59:10Z

Kevin: if the synthetic run reproduces, let's validate the new rule in canary for 24h and collect cost delta. if stable we'll request global roll.

Jules: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/491 (contains rule + recording + grafana JSON draft)

Anna: thanks all, keeping this thread short. i'll post the panel links and the bucket dump after the test. :thumbsup:

Kevin: noted. ready to assist when you start the synthetic load.

Jules: adding tests to ensure we don't trigger on noisy scrapes (recording rules + replay tests).

Anna: closing --- will report back with findings mid-day.
